text:
eli: Heads-up — intermittent NXDOMAIN when pods resolve internal-service.namespace.svc.cluster.local in eu-west, started ~10:30. Affects ~10% of requests. Repro with `dig` inside pod. Anyone touching DNS config?

raj: saw it too, started after a couple of node OS upgrades this morning. `dig +trace` shows some nodes reply via 127.0.0.53 and others via 10.101.0.10 with different answers. Suspect split-horizon caching mismatch between node-local-dns and cluster-dns.

maria: can you paste `cat /etc/resolv.conf` from a problematic pod and from a healthy pod?

eli: problematic pod: `nameserver 10.101.0.10
search namespace.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local`
healthy pod on another node: `nameserver 127.0.0.53` on the node's `resolv.conf` shows systemd stub resolver.

raj: node-local-dns + systemd-resolved combo can lead to two independent caches. We've seen systemd return stale NXDOMAIN if upstream UDP responses are truncated (EDNS0) and the fallback to TCP is blocked by egress rules.

eli: node-local-dns logs show repeated `SERVFAIL` and occasional `no such name` for internal-service. Also seeing `udp size 4096` truncated responses in tcpdump.

maria: quick test — on a problematic node: `dig +tcp @10.101.0.10 internal-service.namespace.svc.cluster.local` — does TCP succeed?

eli: yes, TCP answers consistently, UDP sometimes NXDOMAIN.

raj: confirms here as well. UDP path appears to be getting truncated/modified by our egress LB/NAT; EDNS0 bytes get dropped which causes the authoritative to respond with TC=1. Normally resolver retries over TCP, but our nodes can't reach TCP 53 upstream because our outgoing firewall/iptables denies it. The node-local cache then stores the negative result.

maria: short-term mitigation: allow outbound TCP/53 from nodes to the cluster-dns upstream (10.101.0.10) and clear node-local-dns caches. Command we used on one node: `iptables -I OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT`. Also `kubectl delete pod -n kube-system -l k8s-app=node-local-dns` to clear caches.

eli: applied the iptables allow on one noisy node — NXDOMAIN rate there dropped to ~0.5% vs 10% before. Rolling change to remaining nodes.

raj: longer term: we should fix the egress LB to preserve EDNS0 and not mangle DNS UDP, or move upstream to DoT/DoH between node-local and cluster-dns. Also add a config to node-local-dns to prefer TCP on truncated responses.

oncall-bot: Incident routed to eng-infra @channel — severity: S2. Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/infra/dns-troubleshooting — please post updates.

maria: I'll open a PR to add a short-lived cluster policy to permit tcp/53 from nodes and an alert to fire if NXDOMAIN rate >1% for 5m. Will also file a ticket for LB fix and DoT migration.

raj: thanks, once PR is in we'll monitor for 4h and then work with network infra to update LB. After LB fix we can remove the temporary tcp/53 allow. :thumbsup:

eli: good catch — keeping eyes on it, will report back with metrics in 30m. :thinking:
